claim_statement: For administrative normalization, OT.02 is retained as 1497 ha while 1502 ha remains the 2010 design-area context; current geometry itself is represented by the admitted owner polygon.
guardrail: Neither administrative/design area is the affected compaction area; use the admitted polygon for spatial identity and derive geometry area from that polygon when needed.

claim_statement: For current peilgebied spatial identity, Tollebeek OT.02 is represented by owner feature OBJECTID 232 / GLOBALID c07f3d9b-c063-42c3-ba0a-1ff65a1b9c6a from zzl_Peilgebieden layer Peilgebieden Besluit, status 4 (vigerend definitief), persisted as TOLLEBEEK_OT02_CURRENT in EPSG:28992.
guardrail: Admission is for peilgebied geometry only. It is not affected compaction area; GPGOPPVL=1506 is not admitted as exact geometry area and practice/status-1 or obsolete/status-11 variants are excluded.

claim_statement: Tollebeek OT.02 is a managed polder system and should not default to free drainage in SWAP source-response work.
guardrail: Exact event boundary/control behaviour still requires current operational evidence.

claim_statement: 540 m3/min is the admitted IJsvogel installed-capacity benchmark.
guardrail: Installed capacity is not event-specific available incremental capacity and not total OT.02 effective capacity.

claim_statement: Current effective Kievit operating capacity is unknown; 60 m3/min nominal hardware and 1.44 m3/s historical calculated capacity are retained as different quantities.
guardrail: Do not convert the two values into a simple min/max range; require post-2020 pump curve or telemetry.

claim_statement: Kievit-zone water may be assisted by IJsvogel under extreme conditions, so pump allocation must be represented explicitly rather than with one universal pumped fraction.
guardrail: No default assist fraction or reverse IJsvogel-core to Kievit routing is admitted.

claim_statement: Historical Noordoostpolder SWAP drainage parameters can be used as bounded method priors but not as current OT.02 calibration values.
guardrail: Current drainage geometry and resistance require spatial/current evidence.

claim_statement: Current OT.02 peilgebied geometry is admitted for spatial identity, but representative soil-profile sampling and current compaction-state qualification remain data-gated.
guardrail: Use the admitted polygon as the sampling domain; do not query one convenient location and call it the representative Tollebeek profile, and do not equate peilgebied area with affected compaction area.

claim_statement: A compaction state cannot be converted to one universal crop or hydrological damage coefficient because limiting mechanisms and response magnitude depend on soil/profile properties, weather and boundary conditions.
guardrail: Pathway-specific response relations remain necessary; this claim does not provide a numeric response function.

claim_statement: The project reference state must be contextual and explicitly defined; a field-experiment control or apparently low-compaction soil is not automatically an uncompacted or damage-free counterfactual.
guardrail: Reference selection must remain traceable to the causal question and profile/land-use context.

claim_statement: Hydrological source-response modelling should preserve compacted-layer depth/thickness and the thickness of overlying storage rather than reduce the profile to one compaction scalar.
guardrail: Exact layer resolution and hydraulic functions remain model/configuration decisions requiring qualification.

claim_statement: Runoff qualification for compacted profiles requires sub-daily event forcing; hourly precipitation is a defensible baseline for the documented SWAP studies but not a universal temporal sufficiency rule.
guardrail: Shorter-duration intensity may still matter and water-system routing has its own time resolution.

claim_statement: Plot/profile evidence cannot by itself determine catchment, pump or societal impacts; an explicit transfer and aggregation layer is required between source response and off-site consequences.
guardrail: No generic plot-to-catchment scaling factor is implied.

claim_statement: Soil × land-use classes are a defensible national exposure/aggregation architecture, but process response and valuation remain pathway-specific and must not be encoded as universal coefficients in the class definition.
guardrail: The Graves UK classes and probabilities are precedent only; Dutch classes and response evidence must be constructed independently.

claim_statement: The project must keep private/on-site effects, public-budget expenditure and broader societal/external welfare effects conceptually separate until an explicit valuation relation connects a qualified physical effect to a cost category.
guardrail: Historical cost estimates or accounting expenditures are not automatically current societal welfare losses.

claim_statement: Historical or large-scale numerical studies may be used for context, sensitivity or external comparison but must not become current Dutch model parameters without matching scope and qualification.
guardrail: Preserve source population, crop, climate, time period and modelling assumptions when using benchmarks.

claim_statement: The architecture should be capable of representing multiple soil-service consequences from the same soil-state definition while keeping each response and valuation pathway separately qualified.
guardrail: A common soil state does not imply that crop, nitrogen, carbon and runoff responses share one transfer or uncertainty model.
